reader.requirement: At --std 85, a READ (format 1 or format 2, every access mode) of an indexed file executes only when the file is open in the input or I-O mode; never opened, closed, open OUTPUT or EXTEND, or after a failed OPEN, it is unsuccessful with 47 and neither AT END nor INVALID KEY runs. The witness covers dynamic access only.

edition-consulted.switches: bakes --std (85) into each connector's registration (FileConnector.Edition); no rule of this case reads it except the gates listed

DialectBehavior.IndexedDuplicateKeyStatusSequentialOnly: at 85 a random READ by an alternate key whose next record duplicates it answers 02; from 2002 only a sequential READ does (asked after the 47 guard)
Year < 2002: a dynamic-access READ with AT END and no NEXT is refused (IX.4.5.3 SR5)

reader.edition-search: grep 'Edition|DialectBehavior' over ReadOpenModeGuard/SequentialReadGuard (none) and IndexedConnector.ReadSequential/ReadRandom (the 02 gate only, after the 47 guard)
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for this rule: the 47 guard runs first on both READ formats at every edition; the edition-gated arms on the path concern 02 and SR5, not the open mode
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f20_07 covers dynamic access never-opened and OUTPUT; sequential and random access, the EXTEND mode, READ after CLOSE and after a failed OPEN are not exercised (probed here)

probes.printed: never-opened sequential/random/dynamic indexed files: READ 47, READ NEXT 47, WRITE 48, REWRITE 49, DELETE 49, START 47, CLOSE 42; after OPEN+CLOSE: READ 47, DELETE 49, CLOSE 42; SORT USING XV GIVING SQ (both not open) then OPEN INPUT SQ=00, Q1=K001AAAA; SORT USING SQ GIVING XS (indexed) then OPEN XS=00, S1=00 K001AAAA; MERGE USING XV XS GIVING SQ runs (M1/M2=K001AAAA); failed OPEN INPUT (non-optional absent)=35, then READ NEXT 47, WRITE 48, CLOSE 42
probes.expected: each statement on a file not in an open mode is unsuccessful with its IX.1.3.4 logic-error value (47 READ/START, 48 WRITE, 49 DELETE/REWRITE, 42 CLOSE); SORT/MERGE USING/GIVING and OPEN are the exceptions and run; after a failed OPEN either the 35 or the 4x applies and the implementor picks (IX.1.3.4 GR6)

probes.printed: every blank Table 2 cell: Seq OUTPUT READ 47/REWRITE 49/START 47/DELETE 49; Seq EXTEND READ 47/REWRITE 49/START 47/DELETE 49; Seq INPUT WRITE 48/REWRITE 49/DELETE 49; Seq I-O WRITE 48 (file unchanged: K001, K002, at end 10); Random OUTPUT READ 47/REWRITE 49/DELETE 49; Random INPUT WRITE 48/REWRITE 49/DELETE 49; Dynamic OUTPUT READ 47/READ NEXT 47/START 47/REWRITE 49/DELETE 49; Dynamic INPUT WRITE 48/REWRITE 49/DELETE 49; every X cell used gives 00
probes.expected: Table 2 X cells succeed; blank cells are not permissible and are refused with the IX.1.3.4 4x value (the Seq I-O WRITE cell has no value 1985 assigns, so the 48 is the implementor's choice)

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR1  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1  ["must be open in the input or I-O mode at the time this statement is executed"]
OK  §1985:IX.1.3.4  (1.3.4 I-O Status)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.5f  ["The execution of a READ or START statement is attempted on a file not open in the input or I-O mode"]

reader.notes: Both READ entries ask ReadOpenModeGuard first (IsOpen and mode not OUTPUT/EXTEND), so every access mode and format answers 47 with nothing read; INPUT and I-O READs succeed (S-I-READ, R-I-READ, V-I-READ = 00).

refuter.evidence: Probe q2misc-001: never-opened files, READ AT END/NOT AT END and READ INVALID KEY/NOT INVALID KEY: no phrase runs, status 47, the USE procedure runs; after CLOSE WITH LOCK and a refused OPEN (38) READ answers 47. READ lock phrases (later editions) refused at 85 (q3l3..q3l5, COBOL0900), accepted at 2023. cite: OK §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR1 [must be open in the input or I-O mode at the time this statement is executed].
